brief: Two Goldman notes and the market's reaction to a revenue dispute form the day's arc. Shah's "Divergence" note argues the Treasury selloff, now 98bp of a 108bp 10-year rise and almost entirely real-rate driven, continues until AI borrowing becomes rate-sensitive or another part of the economy breaks first; so far Nasdaq has absorbed a 5.23% 10-year without AI borrowers slowing down. Everything outside AI has already cracked: Russell 2000 underperformance, an S&P-vs-ex-AI gap near 10% in five weeks, and most S&P members falling even as the index sits near a record. Hedge funds have crowded into that resilience, with Mag7 near 22% of prime exposure and semis doubled to about 12%. Then Thursday's stress test: the FT reported OpenAI's annualized revenue near $50bn, $20bn below the figure widely cited, which Goldman's Johnstone attributes to OpenAI reporting revenue net of cloud-partner sales against Anthropic's closer-to-gross basis. Equities bounced on that explanation; credit did not, with Oracle and Broadcom CDS at records and CCC spreads at 1,014bp. CPI next week is flagged as the next test.
